data.completion_memo: Implemented the shared adashi_lib::storage core: typed ProjectStore/ProjectStorage API, project/rules snapshots, opaque change cursors, common errors/conflicts, atomic guarded rule batches and fingerprinted durable idempotency using existing SQLite receipts. Both desktop and MCP resolve the same versioned .adashi/storage.json descriptor through the shared factory. Missing descriptors preserve legacy SQLite; invalid/future/unavailable selections fail before database creation. The transitional SQLite bridge preserves existing paths, canonical identity, per-computer mappings and schema behavior; MCP rule listing already uses a typed snapshot. Documented all remaining task-14 SQLite call sites. Fixed a settings read/write race encountered during this task: reads no longer rewrite/reset settings; explicit writes use atomic replacement and bounded Windows sharing retries. Restored the user's intact 12-project recovery copy after the old MCP build reset registrations. Formal bindings and README/storage contract updated. Validation: 179 Rust library tests passed, 5 pre-existing manual workspace checks ignored; desktop/MCP binaries built; standalone --no-default-features MCP built; two actual MCP processes completed 80 concurrent reads with unchanged database/settings bytes and timestamps and verified unavailable/malformed backend failures without fallback; existing 42-call MCP read-only regression passed. Evidence: target/storage-core/fef0ea9a-99a0-4621-a3c9-759f48b9585a/evidence.json and target/read-only-storage/8ec65a34-91ce-46b5-8e70-8b948b8e1bf4/evidence.json. No text/server adapter, UI storage selector or conversion workflow is claimed; native visual/full-domain parity remain task 15. Changes are in the workspace, not committed.

lines:
Execution order: step 02 of 13. Depends on Adashi task ID 12. Complete this prerequisite before starting.

Scope clarification: this finished task delivered the storage foundation and rules slice. The complete interface is a separate required deliverable in task 24, before task 14 implements SQLite against it.

Phase: shared adapter foundation.

Implement the contract from task 12 in the shared Rust core used by desktop and MCP:
- Add the initial project/rules interfaces, backend factory, project handle, common error/conflict types and lifecycle management.
- Add versioned per-project backend configuration. Existing settings without a backend continue to select the existing SQLite database.
- Make desktop and MCP resolve the same project/backend descriptor. Keep local checkout registration, per-computer paths and secret resolution separate from portable project configuration.
- Register SQLite through a transitional wrapper so the app remains usable while task 14 moves all operations behind the boundary. Reject unavailable backend types clearly; do not silently open or create another store.
- Separate shared domain validation and concurrency policy from backend-specific persistence. Add a reusable conformance harness for snapshots, guarded changes, idempotency and change detection.

Acceptance: both entry points instantiate the same storage core; independent projects can have independent configurations; legacy configuration opens correctly; malformed or unsupported descriptors fail without changing project data. Document the remaining temporary SQLite call sites for task 14.

data.title: Storage 02/13 — Build the shared storage core and per-project backend selection
